To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have used a PD model to simulate the transport of granular materials and have used the results of these simulations to study the effects of adhesion and mixing on the final state of a system and the effects of glidants on the flowability of cohesive powders, as well as to characterize heat transfer in granular beds.
the addition of helper particles can be used to promote either mixing or segregation, and that the addition of glidants can be used to improve flowability.

the addition of Janus particles in a system can be used to control its behavior (i.e. promote mixing or segregation), that glidant particles can be designed to improve the flow properties of a dry powder and that the dominant heat transfer mechanism in a granular bed can be determined using the granular Peclet number.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the flow and transport of granular materials and the development of a theoretical framework for predicting the final state of these systems.
the application of concepts developed in fluid mechanics to granular systems.
the application of concepts from fluid behavior to granular systems.

the use of analogies from fluid mechanics can be very useful to understand and control the behavior of dry cohesive powders.
the use of analogies from fluids can be very helpful in understanding and controlling granular materials.

the analogies between fluid and granular behavior, although not exact, provide a useful starting point to understand the physics of granular materials and to engineer systems that can be used in the industrial processing of granular materials.

granular materials are a rich system that can be studied with a wide range of tools.
the use of fluid analogies in granular systems has proven to be a powerful tool in the study of granular materials.
we use the tools and concepts from fluid mechanics to study granular materials, and we find that there is a lot of similarity between the two.

the application of fluid concepts to granular materials is not as straightforward as one might expect.
